what: triq-serve: the page at / starts the programs of triq on this machine, shows what they print, stops them, and runs the triq tool with commands that are typed. Everything the page does goes through the requests below, each with the header x-triq-token.

requests.GET /api/state: programs.found: the programs that can be started, by name. programs.started: each program started here and not forgotten, with id, what it was told, pid, the runtime it is and how many nodes that has, for how many seconds it has run, whether it is being stopped, how it ended and whether that was a failure, and the last lines it printed. programs.asked: the last commands of the tool that were typed, each told the same way. runtimes: every runtime on the machine, with its pid, how many nodes it has, and in started the id of the program started here that it is, or null for one started elsewhere. said: a count, and what went wrong last.
requests.GET /api/machine: everything the runtimes report, as triq json prints it: each runtime with its pools, the kinds it offers and its nodes, their settings, inputs and outputs.
requests.POST /api/command: {"line": "connect robot/imu/pose desk/viewer/input"} is a line as it is typed in a terminal after triq, split into words as a terminal splits it. The name of a program starts that program, told the rest: answers {"started": n}. Anything else is run by the triq tool: answers {"asked": n}, and what it printed is in programs.asked once it has.
requests.GET /api/usage: what the triq tool says it can be told.
requests.POST /api/start: {"program": "stack-quadcopter", "told": "quadcopter2 --speed 5"} starts the program triq-stack-quadcopter as a process, told those words. Answers {"id": n}. A program may be started while others of it run.
requests.POST /api/stop: {"id": n} stops a program that was started here: its runtime is asked to shut down, or the process is ended if it is no runtime, or if it was asked before and still runs.
requests.POST /api/shutdown: {"runtime": "quadcopter"} asks any runtime on the machine to shut down, also one that was started elsewhere.
requests.POST /api/forget: {"id": n} forgets a program that has ended; {} forgets every one that has.
requests.POST /api/quit: ends triq-serve, and the programs it started.

notes: Two runtimes cannot have one name. A program that is a runtime takes its name as the first word it is told, where it takes one: told nothing, a second of it finds the name taken and ends.
What is asked is done a moment later, and shows in the next state. What could not be done is said in state.said.
